findings.issue: The contract says `--selftest` fails 'when a refusal site in the code names one not there' (and CONTRIBUTING says the same), but nothing in the suite looks at the refusal sites. rd62 compares the docstring's list with the names the CASES pass to `_refused`, and rd63 shows only that `_refuse` raises on one literal it is handed directly. A site with an unlisted name is caught only if some case runs that site. A new exit-2 path that writes its own 'no comparison made' line and returns `result` without calling `_refuse` (code 2, `refusal` None) is invisible to both checks. This is the prose-says-more-than-the-code class again, now in the sentence that claims to end it. Today every site is reached by a case (I traced each name to its case: rd5/6, 7, 12-14, 21/22/30/44/47, 28, 31, 38/44/45/58, 42, 46/59/60, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 57), so nothing is wrong in this tree yet. The gap is in the mechanism.
findings.resolution: Make the site half static. Walk the module's AST and collect the name literal of every `_refuse(...)` call and every `(name, why)` tuple returned by `_prepare`/`_recheck_refusal` (or hold those names in one constant table that the walk reads). Compare that set with REFUSALS in both directions. Also enforce in `compare()` (or `main`) that code 2 implies `result['refusal']` is set, with a case that goes red when a path returns 2 unnamed. Or narrow the two sentences to 'a refusal site a case reaches'.

findings.issue: EXIT CODES gives 1 as 'a line lost', yet `_refuse`'s own ValueError (and any other uncaught exception) leaves `main` as a traceback, and Python exits 1. Probe in a scratch mirror: the 'revision' refusal at :947 renamed to 'unresolvable', then run against a fixture repo with an unresolvable --head, exited 1 with `ValueError: refusal 'unresolvable' is not one the docstring names`. So a contract defect, which is exactly what finding 1 can let through, reads to a gate as a measured loss. The control probe with --repo pointing at a missing directory exited 2 (revision), as stated.
findings.resolution: In `main`, catch an unexpected exception, print it under a listed refusal name (for example `[internal]`, with a case), and return 2, so that 1 means only a lost line. Or state in EXIT CODES that an internal error exits 1 with a traceback.

intent.note: Clause by clause against the task description. 'R19 the hook read the block label at exit, capture it at install': matches. `block = os.environ.get("REACH_DIFF_BLOCK")` at :410 is used by both `write(".start", ...)` :421 and `dump()` :478, and rd49 rewrites the label before exit. 'R32 the recheck must refuse on a different case set and on writers differing in either direction': matches. `RECHECK_PROCESSES` compares silent/untraced/written by multiset equality (:1228-1235), and `case_ids` compares by id, falling back to the count (:1236-1248). rd58 covers more writers, rd44 fewer, rd59 ids, rd60 count. 'the exit/refusal contract is stated once in reach-diff.py's docstring (--help) with one selftest per refusal, CONTRIBUTING.md pointing at --help': matches as written. Every name in the list has an asserting case (rd62 green), and CONTRIBUTING :596-601 now points at --help. The contract text, though, claims a site-level check the suite does not make (finding 1). 'R33 a change limited to non-Python files is measured, exit 2 only when nothing is lost': matches. `same_side` treats only identical bytes, commits or trees as the same; `if result["code"] == 0 and not deciding: return _no_conversion(...)` at :1160; rd50 exits 1 over a data-only change, rd42 refuses no-conversion, rd51 exits 0 under --allow-same. 'R34 ident() keeps paths outside the export root verbatim so children differing only in such a path are told apart': DIVERGES in scope. The diff keeps such a path verbatim only when it is also outside the run's temp and home directories. A path under either becomes `<temp>`/`<home>` (:392-393, docstring :176-182), so two children that differ only in a path under the temp directory are still one key, and the docstring says so. The carve-out is needed, because per-run temp directories differ between any two runs and rd29's same child would otherwise become two keys. So the half to correct is most likely the clause's wording, not the code. The executor's claim describes the diff accurately: 'keeps an absolute path outside the export root and the temp/home scratch dirs verbatim', R19 at :410/:478, R34 at :392-393, and 'no edit was made' to carried work that is present in the uncommitted diff. Its dependants answer holds: CONTRIBUTING points at --help, which `main` answers with `__doc__` (:1431-1433).
